notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is a full primary journal article, The Epistemic Side-Effect Effect, by JAMES R. BEEBE AND WESLEY BUCKWALTER, with Mind & Language, Vol. 25, No. 4 September 2010, pp. 474–498 and copyright 2010. Title, authors, year, journal, volume, issue and pages match the neutral reference. DOI is not printed in the supplied text, so DOI identity is not independently confirmed. Source header names https://osf.io/download/z9v68/. Text spans article pages 474–498 including references; no PDF was supplied. Only es_value_o is assigned; all other fields are placeholders. Target test remains ambiguous: Gradient t (747) = −10.126, p < .001; AON t (689) = −7.692, p < .001. These are distinct scoring analyses of the same experiment, with AON removing zero responses. Section 1.2 prints means, SDs and the two t tests, but no Cohen d. No effect-size conversion performed, no candidate selected, and no N derived from degrees of freedom. Both printed test candidates and their same-test p bounds are retained here for parent review.
